Admit-while-positive admits the crossing request once

A full backlog of a thousand customers' usage settles whole across as many syncs as their time needs, each settling at least a chunk, every item once, and a resend charges nothing again

Late usage of a day that posted posts the difference at the next posting
Fixed, session, rolling, rate, billing-period and lifetime limits read their use from the event store, and an item admitted before a reset counts in the window it was admitted in

A usage erasure that stopped at its events' update, run again, clears them and leaves the history as it was: each event in it once

A fresh standalone server logs one single-use setup link to the console's /admin/setup and advertises the setup, invitation and Team routes; the link creates the owner, whose first sign-in enrolls a second factor and who is the console's operator, and once spent it creates nobody (setup_link_invalid)

A server whose root holds a seeded operator logs no setup link; openrails setup-link issues one that replaces the live link and creates another owner once while operators exist; without the console it refuses

Where email is not configured an operator's invitation of an operator by email, made as the console's Team page makes it, is not sent and is answered 201 with its /admin/invite#invite_code= link; the invitee registers through it at once with the address unverified, enrolls a second factor and is an operator holding the invited root role alone; spent, the link registers nobody else (invitation_not_found); an invite link carries its code as #link_code=

An operator's emailed invitation answers no code; the invitee registers the invited address with the code from the email, which proves it with no second code sent, enrolls a second factor and holds the invited root role, an operator in the console's directory

A root operator's own session holding root:merchants:create creates a merchant through the console's POST /admin/merchants, the operator's provisioning: it answers 201 with the merchant and role owner, the operator holds merchant:owner in its team, the directory lists it, and where Vault holds configuration its display name is written; a name held (resource_conflict), a malformed one (invalid_param) and an unknown field (unknown_field) create nothing

In the console the openrails binary serves, a fresh server's setup link creates the owner, who enrolls a second factor and is asked to name the first merchant (skippable, no display name where a file holds configuration); the merchant is created owned by them, and its overview asks to connect a payment provider, saying where the file declares one

Exact payment key reads its own retained outcome without attributing another payment

Host workers on a composed fleet keep River's job timeout and crash rescue

A session cap lets the crossing request finish and refuses the next until it resets

An overrun settles past capacity unclamped, refuses requests until a refill, and records reached_at once
A delegated invoker is refused and takes nothing
Invokers with the same limits share their windows; another trust level is held against its own
Remote and embedded gates decide with the same code; a warm decision needs no I/O and a view keeps deciding while OpenRails is unreachable
Racing requests on two limits never take more than either limit; eighty taken of a hundred and thirty captured leaves seventy
A lost sync reply and a restart with unsent usage converge once, with and without an outbox; a stopped lease holds nothing
A gate ticket lives across many syncs without a deadline and its capture settles in the session it was admitted in
Gate refusals are verdicts (limit_reached with its reset); what still fits is decided on the gate's view; OpenRails down is ErrUnavailable for a cold customer
Closing a gate settles its usage and clears its in-flight report before its lease would lapse
A spend window that names no currency is in its policy's policy_currency, converted to the request's
A limit counting two meters by weight (output four times input, a large model's output six more) admits and refuses at the weighted total, and settles each count rounded half up
A catalog naming a field a limit does not take (rate_cards) is refused, as YAML and over HTTP, and applies nothing; the one-to-one count applies
Four gates racing a small balance with steady traffic overshoot at most the bound (what the others admit in four sync intervals, plus one request a gate), and every admitted request settles once

Two gates and an unreachable OpenRails keep deciding on their views and together spend at most what was left, each its share; what a flush resends is settled once, and a sync sent in the outage that fails after OpenRails is back fails no flush begun after it
An idle gate stops syncing and its lease lapses out of the gate count; its stale view decides one request and the next waits for a sync
A fixed window that resets between syncs is decided from the view's next window with no sync, and settles there
One billing policy caps what is owed and spend per window, each refusing on its own, and a customer's own credit limit overrides the policy's cap
A customer graduates to the tier its net amount paid reaches, and the tier's billing policy decides its requests

A tier asking a net amount paid and days since the first payment is reached only when both are met
A chargeback or refund lowers the net amount paid and the customer's tier drops with it
A customer's explicit trust level beats the merchant's tier rules, and a request's own trust level picks that request's spend windows

One merchant's failed background pass fails its job after the other merchants finish

PSP import and its queued job commit together

A live Stripe key of the declared account passes the production write gate; one of another account is Mismatched and writes nothing
Expired vault card is updated at its Account Updater, as a new token or a new expiry, and its renewal retries on it

Ahead-of-renewal refresh asks armed vaults about due cards only, including cards awaiting a method, and retries a throttled vault without marking cards checked
PSP-held card declined as expired asks the customer with no refresh
An unmapped NMI plan blocks its subscriptions until a person maps it from the observed catalog; re-apply lands once
A Stripe price the provider deactivated is retired: not a tier-change target, still billing
A plan-less CCBill member lands only on the one PSP price its rebill equals or a person's pick
The pull observes the whole provider catalog read-only, deleted and inline objects included
The Stripe catalog read keeps the newest observation, retires prices of archived or deleted products and skips what it cannot read
Loading PSPs, in one process or another, pulls none; a person pulls each NMI, Stripe and CCBill PSP, history from the earliest object, landing nothing; Solana has no import

A landed Stripe customer attributes a later out-of-band subscription; a customer mapping another keeps it; one another customer holds is a conflict for only its customer

A period in a unit whose volume price falls below what its receipts took is credited at the posting that takes the usage, taking back on its falling line what the period forgave before crediting what the lots paid beyond its price
A lease sync takes usage in a declared unit only
The first balance in a unit waits for the units lock a settings change takes before it locks any customer, and records the unit's scale; a gift in a counted unit takes no lock

An invoice priced in a merchant's unit, paid from lots bought in dollars and euros, has one revenue schedule per paid currency, each funded with exactly the lots' money its spends released: an item recognised at once, a 30-day pass ratably over its window; applying the invoice again makes nothing new, and the schedules move with a billing archive, whose export refuses a leg naming the invoice in money no lot paid it with

A chargeback of a pack whose units paid for a 30-day pass takes the consumed share of its cash from the pass's schedule as a price reduction with catch-up; winning the dispute restores it, its contra and deferred parts each under its own label, and recognition resumes at the restored price
A unit-priced line paid only with given units has no revenue schedule and moves nothing in the general ledger

Money of a lot released into a unit-priced line's schedule after it was made adds to its funding when the invoice is applied again, also when a chargeback took some back and the funding returns to a level it reached before; ledger-audit fails money released under a schedule that does not exist
A $15 refund at Stripe of a $20 pack of 400 GOLD whose 200 GOLD paid for a 30-day pass takes the 200 left and $5 of the pass's schedule against refunds, as a price reduction with catch-up
A full chargeback of a pack whose units paid $5 of usage and a $10 pass takes the $15 it spent pro rata: the pass's schedule to zero and $5 against usage revenue
A statue paid from a dollar lot and a euro lot: a chargeback of the euro pack reduces the statue's euro schedule alone, and the dollar schedule stands

Cash, payments, attempts, purchases and rebills by outcome or kind equal the measures they replace on one merchant's real sales, refund, won dispute, declines and missed renewal, and a measure or dimension the registry does not serve is refused

The health overview is built from what the merchant sells, every profile's overview saves and answers, an empty merchant's tiles answer with no error, the currency switch keeps each currency's money apart, and saved widgets naming a removed measure, or mrr by a dimension it no longer takes, are dropped
Every money measure splits by currency unless one currency is named, by PSP and by time too, and money beside a measure with no currency is refused rather than summed
A sale and usage at 23:30 in a merchant's accounting timezone, ten hours behind UTC, count on that local day: date ranges and day buckets start at its midnights and the result names the zone

A day chart across a midnight clock change has one row per local day, the changed day starting at its transition with the sale made on it; the catalogue marks measures read from rollups kept per UTC date

Two customers over four months: monthly MRR movements and subscriber movements equal the movements recorded; MRR, subscribers, ARPA, LTV, subscriber churn of the opening base by type, NRR and GRR as each month began; churn read monthly by day and over 90 days; the cohort's retention of the members it acquired, by subscribers and MRR; MRR by product at a past date; subscribers counted once across currencies; scheduled churn and its reversal; cancel decisions by the month they were made, type and reversal; the overview's MRR tiles

A card merchant's chargeback ratio tile is Visa's VAMP ratio, naming its program, and Payment health charts the VAMP and ECM ratios against their levels in force each month (VAMP's excessive level 2.2% before April 2026, 1.5% from); one chargeback under VAMP's minimum count reaches no level whatever its ratio

A metrics query's order term it cannot sort by is refused invalid_order on its own order[i] param: both a measure and a dimension, a direction other than asc or desc, a measure it does not ask for, a dimension it does not group by
NMI's own transaction history is no measure: the schema names no nmi_history measure or nmi_kind dimension, and a query naming nmi_history_authorizations is refused unknown_measure
A catalog edit and its history entry commit together, and a refused edit rolls both back
A catalog document records one entry for each object it changes, with its revision and application; a replay records nothing and a removed key is recorded
A configuration change through the API is recorded with its actor, and a credential only as changed, never its value
A Vault document written outside OpenRails is recorded once as Vault's when several replicas load it, and an edited file once as the file's however many processes start on it
The configuration history lists one merchant's entries newest first, by object and time, a page at a time, to merchant configuration readers only
A product's revision shows on its reads, advances on a key change and never on a price change, and its entries carry it
A product edit, archive, key change or delete naming a stale expected revision is refused with revision_mismatch naming the current one, records nothing, and the current revision succeeds

A Stripe chargeback records one dispute with its network, reason family, code and due date, books one reversal, ends the subscription and its access, blocks the card and asks staff to review the customer; replays change nothing
A CCBill chargeback is recorded with its reason, card network and reversal, its outcome unreported
Mastercard's ratio divides a month's chargebacks by the previous month's sales, Visa's by the month's own
The VAMP level in force is the evaluated month's: 2.2% in March 2026, 1.5% from April
A staff refund carries its reason, requested_by_customer unless named; a Stripe dashboard refund carries Stripe's; refunds count in no dispute ratio
A won dispute books its recovery and stays won against a late notice that it opened; a lost one stays lost against a late notice from before the decision

Chargebacks that bring a PSP's ratio to its acquirer limit's warning raise one high finding that alerts; at the limit it escalates to critical and alerts again; sales settling afterwards re-evaluate and resolve it; minimums are actual counts
A charged-back card is never charged again: the customer's other engine subscription on it keeps its paid period and waits for another card, while one on their other card renews on it
A chargeback blocks the card its charge was taken from, never the card the subscription moved to since
A dispute update or an early fraud warning on a charge OpenRails does not know is answered with a finding, never retried

An NMI chargeback batch records every entry with its code: a matched entry is its charge's, reversed, linked and its subscription canceled; an unmatched one takes the masked number's network, books nothing and still counts in the monitor
The network rollup is derived and leaves no row in an archive: a restored book rebuilds it from its payments, disputes and fraud reports, equal to the source's, and its program standings with it

An RDR resolution books one refund (dispute_prevention), whichever of it and Stripe's own refund arrives first, and records the refund it absorbed; a stale inquiry notice reopens nothing; a CE 3.0 block books nothing; neither counts in a ratio

The dispute metrics equal the records: disputes by kind, reason, outcome and the disputed charge's kind, the win rate, the chargeback rate by network, the VAMP ratio with Visa's lines and ECM's with Mastercard's, fraud reports by outcome and refunds by reason; a card merchant's overview carries the dispute programs widget, whose read answers

A Stripe inquiry books, cancels and revokes nothing, its closing undoes nothing, its escalation books the chargeback once, and the reconcile pull records it without proposing it; a chargeback an advisory pull found waits for the merchant to be armed, or for a provider's notice of it

An actionable early fraud warning is a fraud report Visa counts once; without waiting for the merchant's destructive arming it refunds the charge in full once (fraud_warning, fraudulent at Stripe), ends what it paid for and blocks the card whatever events repeat it; one an event calls unactionable is not acted on; a charge in dispute is not refunded; a charge with nothing left to refund is still ended; recording reports only refunds nothing; below a full posture the response waits with one alerting finding and runs when the posture is raised
An unmatched NMI chargeback is attached by the operator
A chargeback of a refunded charge says to contest it
An operation's attempting entry is written before its provider call and outlives the process dying mid-call; recovery only appends
A subscription's history reads its provider operations from the operations history, each entry once with its phase, kind, attempt and attribution
A price key's moves to a new version, an archive and back are configuration history entries with the key's revision, and a price's history reads them
The breaker marks a destructive attempt sent before its provider call, and its phases are written ahead with their actor
A price migration's source archive waits for the catalog lock another writer holds, then is recorded once, as the migration's, with the key's move to nothing
A parked or stale claim never counts as sent: a stale executor marks nothing, and a park of an admitted attempt clears its mark
Each refusal is stored with its outcome, cause and the PSP's and network's advice, approvals with neither, and the attempt list filters by outcome and cause
An NMI catch-all decline is classified by the issuer's code the Query API reports: a never-retry code waits for a new card and never cancels, a retryable one keeps the schedule
A Stripe renewal Radar blocked is the merchant's refusal and waits for a new card; an issuer's fraudulent decline stays the issuer's

Newly mapped codes decline with their cause: NMI 461 is the merchant account's brand, and Stripe's do_not_try_again, new_account_information_available, service_not_allowed, mobile_device_authentication_required, invalid_amount and testmode_decline have their reasons

Mastercard retry-after advice (MAC 24 to 30) delays the next dunning retry; a delay past the case's window keeps the subscription past due, retries at the advised time and recovers, never asking for another card
New card data (MAC 01, confirm_card_data) is update_cardholder_data, and cards that won't recur (MAC 40, 41) wait for a new card

Authorization rate, issuer-discretion decline rate and first-try rebill approval read the stored outcomes and causes: refusals and errors are in neither, missed renewals in neither; the decline mix and Visa categories, and cuts by kind, card brand, BIN, token type and whether the storing transaction's id was sent; the overview shows them as tiles and in Payment health
The system-errors finding counts the rail's own processing errors, not an issuer's failure behind a generic decline
An engine NMI renewal declined with 200 reads the issuer's code after the decline, or from the invoice read when the answer was lost; a failed read keeps NMI's own code
An issuer that keeps deferring past the next renewal leaves the case past due with no retry until that renewal, then ends it exhausted as issuer_deferred
A retry that runs late without advice, past the next renewal, keeps dunning with the attempts the policy has left
A weekly plan whose first decline is advised past its renewal (MAC 30) stays past due with no retry, and ends at the renewal as issuer_deferred
A new card on a case the old card's advice deferred is not held to that advice: its plain decline keeps dunning, and the case ends as the card failed, not issuer_deferred
A monthly plan bought mid-month posts its cash to its PSP's clearing account, defers it, and recognises at the month boundary and the period end
An annual calendar plan recognises a twelfth a month across a leap February; a non-UTC accounting zone's boundary follows DST
Lifetime access is recognised at once, a time-limited pass ratably over its window, and seats are funded per seat
A Stripe invoice with non-cash credit, NMI and CCBill rebills and a Solana pull in USDC book cash to their PSPs and recognise from payment
A seat increase defers its charge over the rest of the period
An idle recognition pass takes no schedule; a replayed boundary or invoice posts once
An external payment books to external_receipts; a payment beyond its bill stays unapplied
An immediate cancellation without a refund forfeits the remainder
A usage invoice's card and remitted payments book their cash and apply it to the usage receivable
Revoked access ends its schedule; an undone revocation takes the forfeit back
A late payment on an expired invoice whose product another invoice holds stays unapplied
A purchase is applied over the access its grant gives; a replay applies an invoice with no schedule
A prune that hides booked money or a recognising subscription raises a finding its undo resolves
An end before the schedule exists reaches it: a charge after a cancellation is forfeited at payment
ledger-audit warns of revenue lines completed before the books started and of a provider's tax line, skips a merchant's own unit, and fails a line completed since
An invoice applied again after a payment sorting earlier arrives applies no payment beyond what it brought
An imported purchase is applied over the access its import grants
A partial refund while the service runs is a price reduction with catch-up
A full refund that revokes access takes unrecognised revenue first
A chargeback reduces its schedule and the won dispute restores it, its deferral forfeited at once
A refund row written past the poster commits; ledger-audit names it and raises a finding
A duplicate capture's refund returns it from unapplied cash
A refund of a payment from before the books is never refused; its sign breach is a finding
A usage invoice's refund is contra revenue, its payment's cash having settled the receivable; its chargeback reopens the owed, receivable again, with no contra
Refunds in pieces each reduce the price from where the last left it
A refund of a two-line bill takes each line pro rata
A mixed credit invoice's refund, chargeback and won dispute move each dollar once: the lot's share first
An end undone after a refund reinstates no forfeit it never made
A refund the rail confirms later is dated in the general ledger when it settled, its credit lot's money with its own; the lot's units left the balance when it was requested
A timed line refunded before its access is granted is not unscheduled
A reversal's share of a credit lot, card credits or a merchant's own unit, is decided when it settles: a refund that found the lot returned takes none of what a won dispute restores
A reversal whose postings, its own and its lot's, move other cash than its amount fails ledger-audit and raises a finding
A usage invoice's payment, the merchant's first receipt, starts the books, so a reversal of it stored past the poster is named
A refund after an early end forfeited revenue takes the forfeit first, and the end undone reinstates only what is left of it
A won dispute's recovery that names no chargeback commits and restores the chargeback that occurred first
A provider's discount on a bill with a credit line reduces the other lines alone: the lot keeps its own price
A refund of a pack of a merchant's unit the books never booked withdraws its units at once, records its share, books its cash against the payment and raises books.credit.unbooked
A refund of a money lot the books never booked withdraws its units to units_refunded at once, records its share, books its cash against the payment and raises books.credit.unbooked
A $50 pack of 55 credits defers its price from its payment; 11 credits release exactly $10 and the last credit releases the remainder
A lapsed pack's unreleased money is breakage, a revoked pack's is forfeited, and reinstating it reverses the forfeit and lets it be revoked again
A gift's spend grosses usage up against promotional credit; owed is receivable and is repaid at face from a gift and from a bonus pack
A refund of unspent credit returns its deferred money, a chargeback of spent credit is contra-revenue, and a won dispute reverses it
An archive with a reinstated pack and a pack from before the credit books restores, each lot keeping its money
A won dispute repays again only owed still outstanding: the rest returns to the balance with its money, and the payment refunds after
Two partial recoveries of a chargeback, with and without reopened owed, follow the units they restore and end exact
Owed that accrued partly before the credit books is repaid through the receivable first and the rest as revenue, from a gift and a pack
Refunds in pieces strand no deferred money, and a merchant-unit lot refunds its units in the unit and its money in its paid currency
A revocation retried under its idempotency key after a reinstatement replays, and a lapsed lot is not reinstated
A credit lot applied beyond its payment's cash fails ledger-audit, as a bill's lines would
A credit lot whose payment brought no cash defers nothing, raises books.credit.unapplied and commits
Staff partial and full refunds of revoked or spent purchased credit return 409 resource_conflict and move nothing
Two billing passes started together: one runs its scans and the other exits without a report; the running pass holds a lease row, not a database session
A billing pass whose holder died leaves a lease that lapses on its own; a pass started meanwhile exits, and the next takes what is due

Deps.ProviderEndpoints sends provider clients only to loopback fakes: a hostname, a non-loopback address, userinfo or a source matching every address refuses New, and so does any endpoint beside a live PSP

Two fleets on one database: neither fails job progress while the other queues the billing pass, its lease live or lapsed; the fleet whose queued pass never runs reports it, and once no fleet has queued one for a day every fleet does

A host whose Vault login is still under way at New: New waits for its first token and the configuration probe never reports Vault refused; a login slower than New's wait is reported as one under way and served once it completes

Behind PgBouncer in transaction mode, two merchants' concurrent statements, transactions, committed custody and catalog applies each run as their own merchant, and no server connection the pooler hands to the next client keeps any openrails setting

Behind PgBouncer, River works through the pooler and listens on a direct session: a job queued through the pooler runs within seconds while producers poll every 30, each worker listens on a direct session, every listener whose session dies is redialed and wakes River again, and OpenRails' periodic passes complete

Behind PgBouncer, a usage policy lock and a billing import lock wait for their holders on direct sessions, a merchant pull lease admits one holder, and four concurrent revocations by an actor allowed two an hour revoke at most two and leave the actor held

Behind PgBouncer with server-side prepared statements off, many concurrent reads of two merchants over four server connections fail none, and New refuses a pooled pool whose statements would be prepared

Of concurrent pulls of one merchant one runs and the others skip, another merchant's pull runs beside it, and a provider refresh waits for the running pull; the pull holds a lease row, not a database session
A pull that runs past one lease period keeps its lease and others still skip; a dead holder's lease lapses on its own and the next pull takes it
A signup under a rebill hold charges and creates its subscription; its first renewal waits with access kept and charges once after the release
A failed renewal's dunning retry waits under a rebill hold and retries after the release
Scheduled usage collection waits under a rebill hold and collects after the release
A rebill hold never holds what a person asks for: a customer's immediate upgrade and a staff refund run
--all-merchants sets every merchant's control; each change is one configuration-history entry with its reason, and an unchanged control records none
Destructive arming is each merchant's own: arming or disarming one leaves the other, and one control arms destructive actions and enforcing pulls
Export leaves the source's writes readonly, restore lands the destination readonly and disarmed, an armed destination is refused, and writes full restores the copy
Unreadable controls deny provider writes, rebills and destructive actions

Six distinct customers can cancel within an hour without a wave finding; card removals past the merchant cap are refused 429 and alert staff once; another customer can still cancel after that cap is exhausted
Every auth setting but auth.keys.path, and local_sign_in and admin_console.issuers, refuse boot as unknown keys from the file or the environment; the key path alone loads
A server whose staff cannot enroll a second factor, a public issuer with no totp.key, is not ready and logs the key to mount; with it mounted the server is ready

GET / answers the service, the binary's version, whether /health/ready says ready (not_ready while draining, still 200) and the paths of the API, its configuration, the console and health, naming no host; HEAD / answers too, and every other unknown path is still not found
A customer search finds the merchant's customers however many people of the host's directory who are not its customers match first
A price created with its product publishes its Solana plan before the catalog transaction: another catalog edit commits while the publication waits on the chain, and a retry binds the same plan
A migration push NMI can never take (a schedule on a named plan, or one stating no plan_payments) blocks its move with a finding, settles its migration and is never sent again
A price migration archives its sources as a catalog edit: a later catalog document still declaring a source on sale reports the conflict and does not sell it again

A migration of 101 CCBill subscribers admits every one before reading any, blocks the first page with its creation and the rest by its page job, records cancel_at_period_end without canceling any, and a second migration past the actor's ceiling is refused whole
A Solana subscriber's move is blocked, its migration settles, and nothing is sent to the chain
A migration by price key moves every earlier version's subscribers with a price-change notice; one to another product sends a plan-change notice naming it and applies at renewal
Canceling a migration whose Stripe move was pushed lists the subscription in rail_release_required and leaves Stripe's schedule in place
A creation interrupted while reaching its subscribers records nothing, not even the moves it made, and its retry moves everyone once and answers again with the same migration
InvoicePayment reads back a pay whose answer was lost with getInvoicePaymentAttempt under its key, and retries a pay that never arrived under the same key: one attempt
InvoicePayment reads a Solana invoice awaiting its wallet and confirms it at most twice a minute, well under the purchase limit
A kept customer search lists the contact whose username is the query first, then the newest customers, and the list keeps that order
A customer's verified email in the token it presents is its kept contact, and its receipt is sent there
Token claims keep no unverified email, replace only undated claims, and never undo a directory's dated push or an erasure
On a standalone server, the verified email a merchant's backend asserts for its own customer is that customer's contact
A CCBill postback names its customer by a username more than one search's worth of the host's users contain, not leaving it unattributable
A migration's subscribers and the source it archives are one destructive command: staff one unit short is refused whole, nothing recorded or archived; at exactly the limit it succeeds with no hold
A cancel ends a migration's walk whose next page never ran: it is no longer preparing, the subscriber it never reached counts as skipped, and the page's job, run later, changes nothing
Two identical creates waiting on the catalog lock answer the one migration, recorded once
A price migration whose caller leaves after its source is archived is still recorded, and the identical retry answers it under the one command: two subscribers and the source, admitted once

An identical price migration created while the first records is refused at once with price_migration_in_progress, another destructive command of the merchant is admitted meanwhile, and once recorded the identical request answers it
Running charges bill on the merchant's usage_billing terms with no host setting and no event store: PostgreSQL alone bills them
A customer's admin balance and own summary show the billing mode the gate admits it under: prepaid without a card, arrears with one under the merchant's usage terms
Two engines starting together on a fresh schema and a fresh ClickHouse database take turns migrating it: each migration is recorded once, one store identity, and both serve usage
Usage history is UTC quarter hours grouped into the accounting zone's days as it is read: a 25-hour day holds its 25th hour, depletion burn reads the same days, and a zone change regroups all of it
A usage item whose metadata is longer than 1,024 bytes of compact JSON is refused alone with invalid_param metadata; the rest of the sync settles

With no clickhouse.url and nothing on the default's port, the standalone server serves with usage off and logs one line saying so; a clickhouse.url the operator names that does not answer keeps it from serving

A sync past its usage budget after a chunk starts no other: it answers through_n at the chunk's end, leaves the rest neither settled nor refused (a gap past them too), and the next sync continues there, refusing an item alone and the gap once all before it settled; a resend answers both settlements from their receipts
Usage settled past the balance is pending, then posts the balance and leaves the rest owed
A resend after a lost reply is answered from the lease's receipts and adds nothing to pending
A sync that failed before its commit inserted nothing; the resend adds each item to pending once, priced from the period's start, and the store counts each once
A posting before the resend leaves usage a failed sync did not settle to the resend, which adds it to pending once; the next posting takes it once
A resend older than the lease's kept receipts is covered by its settled number and settles nothing again
Usage owed beyond the balance is usage revenue receivable as it posts; a card collection and remittances settle the receivable in the general ledger
A waived usage invoice takes its revenue back; an uncollectible one carries an allowance for doubtful accounts that comes back as it is collected, or is written off when it is waived

Units owed equal the general-ledger usage receivable after a usage posting, a running charge, a remittance, a gift's repayment, an allowance and a waiver, and after a chargeback whose reopened owed is billed at once and collected again, even once usage terms are withdrawn

A running charge's owed is receivable as it posts and credit repays it at face; a collection settles the receivable and counts owed from before the books as revenue, which ledger-audit warns of until then

A chargeback of a usage invoice's payment owes again what it paid, in both books, once, and its card's rounding change is a loss; the reopened owed is billed and collected again, and the dispute won after that gives the loss back and is the customer's credit at face for the rest, with nothing left unapplied

A merchant's refund of a usage invoice's payment, made through OpenRails or observed from the provider, records and leaves its owed settled; a chargeback after a refund owes again only what the refund left, keeps it if the refund settles later, and its won dispute settles it and gives the loss back
Checkout steps are recorded where the customer takes them: created, opened on the first read in person, submitted on the first pay request, paid
A merchant's pay URL is opened only when its page reads it; an expired checkout is abandoned at the step it reached
A checkout's purchase number counts the customer's paid purchases; an abandoned checkout is not one
A checkout's country is its billing address, then the trusted proxy's IP country, never the address; an untrusted header is ignored
A checkout's language is the first in-person request's Accept-Language, canonicalized
Checkout attribution is normalized and bounded, a bad field dropped without refusing the sale, kept first, and the referrer keeps only its host
An unpaid checkout that never started an attempt keeps its facts for 397 days, then is deleted
A subscription's renewals, and an upgrade's, name the checkout that bought it, whose country and attribution they carry

Checkout measures read the funnel as it happened: checkouts by step and outcome, conversion, submission and customer conversion rates, sales by purchase number, repeat purchase rate, and cash by country and source; the overview's checkout section answers and saves
A checkout's customer type is new on a first purchase, returning after one or while subscribed, reactivated once a subscription ended; sales and cash split by it
Spending a merchant's units is not a checkout: unit invoices carry no checkout facts and leave the funnel, conversion, purchase numbers and repeat purchases to purchases in money
A customer's erasure clears every attribution field of its checkouts; the checkouts stand
A customer cannot cancel a usage invoice or one the merchant created: both answer 409 invoice_not_cancelable and stay open, the usage stays owed to that invoice, and the merchant cancels its invoice
Buying a consumable product again raises no duplicate-ownership finding; a second live purchase of a non-consumable still does
Definitive NMI gateway refusals reopen the invoice with the response taxonomy, without card-decline attempts or a retained new-card vault
A sale that never connects ends uncharged and reopens the invoice
Client disconnect leaves the provider sale running to one paid invoice
An empty NMI order releases after 24 hours, passes sale archive validation, and the merchant can cancel the reopened invoice or let it expire
Operator attestation releases an empty NMI order and refuses an order containing a transaction or an intent holding a paid receipt without changing its evidence

An approved new-card sale grants paid access while card storage retries without another charge; late storage records one reusable card agreement and offers the saved card, and a paid replay preserves revoked reuse consent
A CCBill PSP that declares a webhook token refuses a delivery without it or with a wrong one, and the right token from outside CCBill's addresses: a forged renewal extends nothing
A rotated-out CCBill webhook token verifies only inside its overlap
A CCBill PSP without a webhook token takes the tokenless URL as before and refuses the token URL
require_webhook_token false admits a tokenless CCBill delivery but never a wrong token
The webhook token URL exists only for CCBill: any other rail answers route_not_found

A tokenless CCBill delivery that one PSP of the account refuses for want of its token is refused for all of them, never accepted under a sibling PSP without a token; the right token reaches its own PSP
Rotating a CCBill webhook token over the API keeps the old one verifying for its overlap only, and a supplied previous token is refused
A Solana renewal pull that is confirmed and not finalized books nothing, extends nothing and is not signed again; it is booked once when it finalizes
A first Solana subscription payment that is confirmed and not finalized enrolls nothing and stays pending; it enrolls once when it finalizes
A confirmed Solana pull whose fork is dropped books nothing and is signed again only after its blockhash provably expired

A CCBill rebill callback stamped before the windows already read, which no DataLink read lists, raises one high pull.charge.unconfirmed finding with its payment's evidence 36 hours after it was received; the payment is kept and later refreshes do not duplicate it
A CCBill rebill callback whose transaction a DataLink read lists raises no finding
A genuine CCBill rebill DataLink lists late, in a later window and without its leading zero, raises no finding; an unconfirmed one is resolved by the read that later lists it
An unlisted CCBill rebill callback raises nothing for 36 hours after it was received, and is raised after
A CCBill failed-rebill cancel callback that cut paid access short, for a member the DataLink roster lists active, raises pull.subscription.mismatch at critical and restores nothing
A CCBill rebill DataLink dates hours before its callback's stamp, in an earlier window, raises no finding
An ordinary CCBill cancellation the roster still lists keeps the mismatch below critical until the roster still lists it 48 hours after access ended
A paced (live) CCBill refresh, a day of transactions an hour, raises pull.charge.unconfirmed only for the callback rebill no read lists
A CCBill rebill callback reusing a transaction id DataLink lists under another subscription is raised, with that listing as evidence
A second CCBill rebill callback inside a settled cycle, its next renewal date a day off the accepted cadence, is kept as an extra capture of that cycle, not refused with a 500

An NMI provider price declaring its plan's terms takes them, unconfirmed, while NMI does not answer and is confirmed when it does; NMI's terms win over a declaration that differs, which the receipt reports; a plan stating no terms is still refused, and none states a trial

The console's overview of a merchant none of whose PSPs is armed shows the setup step Connect a payment provider to take payments, which leads to its PSPs page where Vault holds configuration; once a PSP is armed (its list answers armed) the step is gone and the PSP reads active
An hourly usage series across a clock change has the local day's 25 hours, the repeated 01:00 twice, each its own usage; by day the same window is one bucket

A day series in Asia/Kolkata puts usage at 23:45 and 00:15 there, one UTC hour, on two days: history's quarter hours make a half-hour offset exact; the report agrees, and without a zone both are on the merchant's UTC day

Usage whose raw events expired after 90 days stays in the usage series from history; read by invoker, the series and the report refuse a window before the raw events with usage_events_expired, and answer within them
A usage series of more than 1,000 buckets is refused 400 too_many_buckets on interval; a month by hour is answered; an unknown interval is invalid_query
GET /v1/me/usage/series answers only the signed-in customer's usage whatever the query names; staff read the same series with GetUsageSeries, and a customer's token cannot

Usage is taken into history at intake's price; a volume tier's fall is the report's and the bucket's discount, in the hour of the usage that crossed the band, so the report and series less it equal what the period posted
Failed usage is counted on its bucket's one event row (failed_requests, failed_amount, forgiven), never a row of its own; the report counts both items and metrics still split them by outcome
An item settled days after its admission, its limit window over, settles without error and counts toward no window: no limit_usage row and no window row; usage admitted now counts in its live window

A posting takes exactly what is pending, priced on the period's total: two gates' usage across a graduated band posts the price their running totals held, folded into the period's posted row, and leaves nothing queued

Usage reported after a credit lot lapsed, from either side of the lapse, is split at it in the running totals: the posting before the lapse draws the lot for the usage before it only, and the rest is owed

A store that refuses a sync's insert after its commit is tried again: once it takes the usage each item counts once; one that refuses every try still answers the receipts and charges each item once, counting none of them, and a resend inserts nothing
A failed item's grace counts each failure once: the resend of a sync that failed reads no copy of its own failure, and a later chunk of one sync counts the failures of the chunks before it
The balance watch's burn rate reads usage history's quarter hours once each has ended: a look inside the quarter hour sees none of it, the next look all of it, once

Operator settles an NMI renewal from its definitive order decline
Stripe engine renewals reject operator receipt and nonexecution resolution
Stuck renewal verification grows with submission age up to two hours without consuming execution attempts
A renewal submitted long after admission starts verification with the handler backoff
A submitted renewal with an unknown answer keeps access under suspend, including a late submission, then follows payment or dunning
Operator release of an unanswered renewal restores bounded suspend access while rebills are held

An upgrade keeps every usage receipt an earlier build wrote: each line takes its receipt's period and its share of what the receipt forgave, by the amounts of its lines of that sign, to the largest remainder
